[reasoning_validity/major] D1 [criteriaAssessments C1 strengths[0] and mechanisms; counterarguments[0].response] The draft calls the migration/decommission entry (E2) and the INC-2291 shard failover (E4) 'two separate' and 'two independent changelog facts' that corroborate the replicated topology. Both come from the same three-line document (sources/platform-changelog-2025.md), which the packet itself describes as an unconfirmed excerpt. They agree with each other, but that is internal consistency within one source, not independent corroboration. If the excerpt is wrong or out of date, both facts fail together. Calling them independent overstates how strong the evidence is for C1, the criterion the whole verdict rests on.

[traceability/major] D2 [alternatives[3].comparison ('Increase to 2 replicas per shard'); counterarguments[1].response; C3 assessment] The draft says 'the observed problem was client-side error handling (E4, E5)' and treats the client retry gap as the cause of the INC-2291 errors. The source only records an action item ('client retry/backoff on MOVED/failover errors (OPEN)'). It does not name a root cause. The 41s failover window, which may be tunable on the server side (E7), is an equally plausible contributor. The draft states as observed fact something it has inferred, and uses it to rank client retry above the replica-count and failover-tuning alternatives.
